:::{#thm-density-vs-CDF}
#### A density integrates to the CDF

If $X$ is a continuous random variable with density $f$ and CDF $\cdf$,
then for every $t$:

$$\cdff{t} = \int_{-\infty}^{t} f(x)\,dx$$

:::

::: proof

For any $a < t$,
$\{X \le t\}$ is the disjoint union of $\{X \le a\}$ and $\{a < X \le t\}$,
and $\Pr(X = a) = 0$ because $X$ is continuous.
So:

$$
\ba
\cdff{t}
&= \Pr(X \le a) + \Pr(a < X \le t)
&& \text{(additivity, and the definition of the CDF)} \\
&= \cdff{a} + \Pr(a \le X \le t)
&& \text{(definition of the CDF; } \Pr(X = a) = 0 \text{)} \\
&= \cdff{a} + \int_a^t f(x)\,dx
&& \text{(definition of the density)}
\ea
$$

Letting $a \to -\infty$, $\cdff{a} \to 0$ (@thm-cdf-properties),
which gives $\cdff{t} = \int_{-\infty}^{t} f(x)\,dx$.

:::
